english_titles: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II
label: 7 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception II

lines.japanese:
その頃、屋敷は大きな遊び場だった。
　深い森のような庭。
　高い城のような家。
　何日かかっても探険しきれない閉じた箱庭の世界で、ボクたちは遊びまわった。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Back then, the estate was one enormous playground.
A garden as deep as a forest.
A house as tall as a castle.
We ran wild through that little walled-off world, too vast to explore even if we spent days trying.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
Back then, the whole mansion was like a giant playground.
The garden, a deep forest.
The house, a tall castle.
We played in our own little world, which would take days to explore.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
毎日は楽しかった。
　おとなになるなんてこともしらなかったし、
　朝と夜はおんなじようにくりかえされるんだってうたがいもしなかった。
　それは、ただ、子犬のようにはしゃぎまわった幼年期。
　ボクらはとても気が合って、最高の遊び仲間だった。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Every day was fun.
We didn’t even know we would grow up someday,
and never doubted that morning and night would go on repeating themselves forever.
It was childhood, nothing more: the years when we tumbled about like puppies.
We understood each other perfectly and were the best playmates in the world.

It was just a childhood spent playing like puppies.

lines.japanese:
ふりむけばいつもあきはがいて、手をふるとはずかしがって隠れてしまう。
　うん、そんなのもいつもどおり。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Whenever I looked back, Akiha was there, and if I waved, she grew shy and hid.
Yes, that was the way it always was.
lines.mao_english:
Whenever I looked back, Akiha was there, and if I waved, she grew shy and hid.
Yes, that was the way it always was.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Whenever I turned back, Akiha would be there, waving her hands and hiding shyly.
Yes, always the same.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: In Shiki's repeated childhood memory, Akiha is always behind him; when he waves to her, she grows shy and hides. mirror moon assigns both actions to Akiha, so she waves and then hides. The agency reversal recurs across all four cited route instances and changes the small ritual through which Shiki recalls reaching out to his sister.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Shiki waving to Akiha becomes Akiha waving and hiding

lines.japanese:
うっすらと意識が覚醒する。
　朝の光が体を包んで、眠りが少しずつ覚めていく。
　その中で。
　なにか、懐かしい夢をみた気がしていた。
「―――――――」
　目を覚ましたとたん、厭なモノが視界に入ってくる。
　ずきり、とこめかみには銃創のような頭痛。
「く――――」
　急いで枕もとのメガネをかけた。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Awareness slowly returns.
Morning light enfolds my body, easing me little by little out of sleep.
In that half-waking haze.
I felt as though I had dreamed of something long ago.
“―――――――”
The instant I open my eyes, something hateful enters my sight.
Pain punches through my temple like a gunshot wound.
“Ghh――――”
I hastily put on the glasses beside my pillow.

lines.mirrorMoon:
I slowly awaken and open my eyes.
The morning light wraps around me and my sleepiness starts to lift.
As the last vestiges clear,
I sense that I had a very nostalgic dream.
"-------"
As soon as I open my eyes, I start to see those terrible things jump into my vision.
My head stabs with pain.
"Gg----"
I scramble for the glasses by my pillow and put them on.

lines.japanese:
「は―――――あ」
　深く深呼吸をして、なんとか気分を落ち着けた。
「なんだって―――朝から、こんな」
　こんな、はっきりと線を見てしまったのか。
　建物の死の線は見えにくい。
　見えていてもそれはうっすらとしているし、今のようにはっきりと見える事は稀だったのに。
「…………」
　くわえて、今は『点』まで見えてしまっていた。
　なんだか頭痛も鋭くなっている気がする。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah―――――ah”
I take a deep breath and somehow steady myself.
“Why―――am I seeing them this clearly first thing in the morning?”
Why did I see the lines so clearly?
The lines of death on buildings are hard to see.
Even when visible, they are faint; it is rare for them to stand out as sharply as they do now.
“…”
Now I can even see the “points.”
The headache feels sharper too.

lines.mirrorMoon:
I take in some air.
After taking a few deep breaths, I manage to calm down.
"Why did I----so early…"

It's usually hard to see them, and seeing them so clearly like I just did now is rare.
"…………"
What's more, I even saw those "points".
I think my headache is getting worse too.

lines.japanese:
先生は、この目がよくないものを呼び寄せる、と言っていた。
　アルクェイドや吸血鬼といったものは、確かによくないものだと思う。
　なら、相乗効果というヤツでこの両目も力を増していってしまっているのかもしれない。
「――――まさか」
　たぶん、ただ疲れているだけだろう。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
My teacher once told me these eyes would draw dangerous things to me.
Arcueid and vampires certainly qualify.
Maybe some kind of vicious feedback is making the eyes themselves grow stronger.
“――――No way”
I am probably just tired.

lines.japanese:
「あれ────？」
　そういえば、翡翠の姿がない。
　時刻は朝の七時過ぎだ。
　いつもなら翡翠がやってきていて、起きるように呼びかけている時間なのに。
「……寝坊したのかな、翡翠」
　そのわりには、机の上にキチンと着替えの制服が用意されていたりする。
「なんだろ。
なにか他の仕事でもあったのかな」
　気にはなるが自分には関係のない事かもしれない。
　今朝は時間もないし、手早く制服に着替えて居間にむかった。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
“Huh────?”
Come to think of it, Hisui is not here.
It is already past seven.
Ordinarily she would have arrived by now and be trying to wake me.
“Did Hisui oversleep…?”
And yet my uniform has been laid out with perfect care on the desk.
“I wonder what happened. Maybe she had some other work to do.”
It bothers me, but it may have nothing to do with me.
I’m short on time this morning, so I dress quickly and head downstairs to the sitting room.

lines.japanese:
「――――――あ」
　ロビーから居間に入ろうとして、とんでもない事を失念していた事に気がついた。
　扉を開けて、居間に一歩も足を踏み入れられず立ち尽くす。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――Oh”
Just as I am about to enter the sitting room from the foyer, I remember the catastrophe I had somehow forgotten.
I open the door—and freeze on the threshold, unable to take a single step inside.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"------Ah."
As I go from the lobby towards the sitting room, I realize I forgot something terribly important.
I open the door and stand there, without taking a single step forward.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
居間には秋葉がいた。
　傍らには琥珀さんもいて、二人は無言で紅茶を飲んでいる。
　いつもはどんなに刺があろうが
「おはようごさいます、兄さん」
　と挨拶をしてくる秋葉さんは、今朝にかぎってこっちを見てもくれない。
「あ…………う」
　言うまでもなく。
　昨夜、アルクェイドが屋敷にやってきた一件が尾を引いている結果である。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Akiha is in the sitting room.
Kohaku is beside her, and the two of them are drinking tea in silence.
No matter how barbed her mood,
Akiha always greets me: “Good morning, Brother.”
This morning, she will not even look my way.
“Ah, uh”
There is no need to ask why.
Arcueid’s visit to the estate last night is still casting a very long shadow.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Akiha is in the sitting room.
Kohaku-san is nearby and the two of them are drinking tea silently.
Normally she would say,
"Good morning, Nii-san,"
no matter how angry she might be, but she doesn't even look at me this morning.
"Ah……… uh."
It goes without saying.
Arcueid's coming here last night has some very lasting repercussions.

秋葉のいらいら加減はハンパじゃなくて、居間は打てば響くような緊張感に支配されている。
「おはようございます、志貴さん」
　……まあ、それもこの人だけにはまるで影響を与えていないみたいだけど。
「あ…うん、おはよう琥珀さん」
　琥珀さんに片手をあげて、居間に入る。
lines.label: s143
lines.maoEnglish:
Akiha’s irritation is off the scale, and the tension in the room is so taut it would ring if struck.
“Good morning, Master Shiki.”
None of this seems capable of troubling Kohaku.
“Ah, yes, good morning, Kohaku.”
I raise one hand to her and venture into the room.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Akiha's irritation is permeating the air.
You could practically cut the tension with a knife.
"Good morning, Shiki-san."
…… Well, it seems like she's remained unaffected, at least.
"Ah… yeah, good morning Kohaku-san."
Raising a hand to Kohaku-san, I enter the sitting room.

とことこと足音を忍ばせて歩く俺に、秋葉はじろりとした流し目を向けてきた。
 ───うう、無言の圧力なんかに負けないぞ。

lines.maoEnglish:

───I will not be cowed by a little silent pressure.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: In Shiki's repeated childhood memory, Akiha is always behind him; when he waves to her, she grows shy and hides. mirror moon assigns both actions to Akiha, so she waves and then hides. Fortunately, Kohaku recognized you and switched off the alarm; otherwise Shiki Tohno would be sitting in a police cell right now.”

Partway through her speech, Akiha’s cheeks redden and she turns away.
───So Akiha thinks Arcueid and I are lovers.

lines.japanese:
「待て秋葉。
いっとくけどな、俺とアイツの間には何もないぞ。
ただアイツの探しモノに手を貸してやってるだけなんだ。
用が済めば二度と会わない関係なんだよ、俺たちは」
「へえ。
そのわりにはずいぶんと親しそうでしたけど、それは私の気のせいだって言うんですね、兄さんは」
　秋葉の視線は冷たい。
　……そんなコトはない、なんて嘘を言ってしまえば楽なんだろうけど―――秋葉に嘘を言うのは気が引けるし、なにより、アルクェイドとは親しくないなんていうのは、なんかすっごくイヤだった。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hold on, Akiha, there is nothing between us. I am only helping her find something. Once that is done, we will never see each other again. That is all there is between us.”
“Really? You seemed remarkably close, yet you are telling me I imagined it, Brother?”
Akiha's gaze is cold.
It would be easy to lie and deny it―――but I hate lying to Akiha, and more than anything, I hate the idea of claiming Arcueid and I are not close.

Akiha's gaze is cold.
It would be easy to lie and deny it―――but I hate lying to Akiha, and more than anything, I hate the idea of claiming Arcueid and I are not close.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Wait, Akiha.
There's really nothing between us.
I'm just helping her find something.
After that, we won't even see each other again."
"Oh really?
You certainly seem very close.
That must be my imagination, right Nii-san?"
Her gaze is cold.
…… If I lie with something like "That's not it," things will be much easier, but---more than the fact that I don't want to lie to Akiha, I really don't want to say that we aren't close.

lines.japanese:
「――――う。
それは、その……秋葉の気のせいじゃ、ないかも」
「でしょうね。
兄さんは今までみた事もないほどあわててたもの。
何事も真剣になってくださらない兄さんが感情を顕にするなんて、どういう風の吹き回しなんでしょうね」
「そんな事はないよ。
ただアイツが家に来るなんてまったくの不意打ちだったから驚いていただけだろ」
「あの女の人は落ち着いた様子で兄さんの事をずっと待ってましたけど」
　秋葉は不機嫌そうに横目で俺を睨む。
　どうも秋葉は俺とアルクェイドが付き合っている、と信じ込んでしまっているようだ。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――Urk. Well, perhaps you did not imagine it.”
“I thought not. I have never seen you so flustered. You never take anything seriously, so what on earth made you show your feelings so openly?”
“It was not like that. I was only shocked because her arrival at the estate caught me completely off guard.”
“She looked perfectly composed while she waited for you.”
Akiha glares sideways at me.
She seems utterly convinced that Arcueid and I are dating.

"----That, may not…… be your imagination, maybe."
"Right.

I was just totally caught off guard that she'd actually come here."
"That woman calmly waited for you the whole time, Nii-san."
She casts a sideways glare at me.
She really seems convinced that Arcueid and I are dating.

lines.japanese:
「あのな、秋葉。
勘違いもそこまでにしとけよ。
そもそも俺とアイツが知り合ったのは───」
　俺がアイツを殺したからなんだ、と言おうとして口を塞いだ。
　……いくらなんでも本当の事を言うのはあまりにバカげてる。
　かといって他にうまい言い訳も考えつかず、昨夜に引き続きムニャムニャと言葉を濁すしかなくなった。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“Listen, Akiha, that is enough. You have got this all wrong. The whole reason she and I met was───”
I nearly say that I killed her, then clamp my mouth shut.
The truth is far too absurd to tell.
Unable to invent a convincing excuse, I mumble and trail off as I did last night.

In the first place, we first met---"
by me killing her, but I swallow the rest of those words.
…… It'll be too stupid to tell the truth.
But I can't even think of a good excuse, and I can only stammer.

lines.japanese:
「答えられないのでしたら質問を変えましょうか。
さきほどから兄さんはアイツアイツと繰り返していますが、あの人の名前はなんていうんです？」
「……その、アルクェイドっていうんだけど」
「そうですか。
という事はお知り合いになったのは学校ではありませんね。
兄さんの高校には留学生はいませんから」
「……うっ」
　秋葉の言うとおり、うちの高校には外国からの留学生なんてのはいやしない。
　いやしないんだけど、どうして秋葉はそんなことまで知ってるんだろう？
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“If you cannot answer, shall I change the question? You have called her ‘that woman’ over and over; what is her name?”
“Her name is Arcueid.”
“I see. Then you did not meet her at school. There are no foreign exchange students at your high school.”
“Urk.”
Akiha is right; our school has no foreign exchange students.
But how does she know even that?

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Akiha explicitly notices Shiki repeatedly referring to Arcueid with the marked aitsu, 'that woman' or 'her,' and asks for the stranger's name. mirror moon says he has repeatedly called her the ordinary pronoun 'her,' which is neither a name nor a conspicuous form of address. The translation erases what Akiha heard and leaves her question without its trigger in three branches.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Akiha noticing Shiki's repeated 'that woman' becomes an impossible comment about 'her'

「街で知り合ったんだよ。
その、偶然」
「ふぅん、偶然ですか。

「あ───いや、声をかけたのは、俺のほうだけど……」
　実際は声をかけたわけじゃないけど、知り合うきっかけを作ったのはこっちのほうだ。

“Then where did you meet a woman like her?”
“In town. It was a coincidence.”
“A coincidence, was it? Then Arcueid must have approached you.”
“Ah───no, I was the one who approached her…”
Strictly speaking, I did not call out to her, but I created the occasion for us to meet.

「どうして声をかけたんです？
　兄さんはアルクェイドさんとは何もないのに。
それとも初めはそういうおつもりだったんですか？」
　秋葉の質問は、実に的確だ。
　一歩ずつ確実にこっちの急所へ近付いてくる。
　これじゃあ蛇に睨まれたカエルみたいなもんで、じき誤魔化しのきかないところまで追い込まれてしまうだろう。
　ここはもう、強引にでも話を終わらせるしかない。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“Why did you approach her? You say there’s nothing between you and Arcueid. Or was that what you wanted from the beginning?”
Akiha’s questions are unerringly precise.
Step by step, she is closing in on the most vulnerable point.
I am a frog transfixed by a snake; before long, she will have me cornered where no evasion can save me.
I have no choice but to force an end to this conversation.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Why did you talk to her?
I thought Arcueid-san was nothing to you.
Or did you only intend it like that from the beginning?"
Her questions are right on the mark.
Step by step, she draws closer to my secret.
Like a snake staring at a frog, she ignores all my excuses and is trying to drive me into a corner.
I can now only use force to end this conversation.

「ああもう、とにかくアイツとは何でもないんだって！
　だいたいな、俺が何をしようが秋葉には関係ないだろ。
俺が誰と付き合おうが文句を言われる筋合いはないはずだ」
　びしっ、と秋葉を指差して言い捨てる。
　秋葉はむっ、と顔をしかめた後────すぅ、と音もなく立ち上がった。
「────？」
　……おかしいな。
　てっきり怒鳴り返してくると思ったんだけど、秋葉は逆に気まずそうに視線をそらした。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh, enough; there is nothing between us!
Besides, whatever I do is none of your business. You have no right to complain about whom I choose to date.”
I thrust an accusing finger at her and deliver the verdict.
Akiha scowls, then────rises soundlessly to her feet.
“────?”
That is strange.
I expected her to shout back, but instead she looks away, oddly self-conscious.

lines.japanese:
「……私だって、こんな事を言いたくありません。
ただ、あの人は厭な感じがするんです。
　他の相手なら仕方がないって諦める。
けど、兄さんがあの人に懸想しているっていうんなら、なんだか私が罵迦みたいじゃないですか」
　……どうしてだろう。
　秋葉は悔しそうに、唇をかんで、そんな事を言った。
lines.label: s146
lines.maoEnglish:
“I do not want to say any of this either. There is simply something about that woman I cannot stand.
If it were anyone else, I would accept it and give up. But if you have truly fallen for her, then I feel like an utter fool.”
Why?
Akiha bites her lip and says it, looking bitterly frustrated.

「そうですか。

Besides, whatever I do is none of your business. You have no right to complain about whom I choose to date.”
I thrust an accusing finger at her and deliver the verdict.
Akiha scowls, then────rises soundlessly to her feet.
“────?”
That is strange.
I expected her to shout back, but instead she looks away, oddly self-conscious.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"That's enough.
I said she's nothing to me!
Besides, whatever I do doesn't concern you.
You don't have any right to complain about who I date, anyway."
I point at her directly.
After giving an angered face----she stands up without a sound.
"----?"
…… That's odd.
I thought she would yell back at me, but instead she appears very uncomfortable and looks away.

lines.japanese:
「……私だって、こんな事を言いたくありません。
ただ、あの人は厭な感じがするんです。
　他の相手なら仕方がないって諦める。
けど、兄さんがあの人に懸想しているっていうんなら、なんだか私が罵迦みたいじゃないですか」
　……どうしてだろう。
　秋葉は悔しそうに、唇をかんで、そんな事を言った。
lines.label: s148
lines.maoEnglish:
“I do not want to say any of this either. There is simply something about that woman I cannot stand.
If it were anyone else, I would accept it and give up. But if you have truly fallen for her, then I feel like an utter fool.”
Why?
Akiha bites her lip and says it, looking bitterly frustrated.

lines.japanese:
四時限目の授業は現代社会だ。
　昼休み前ということで教室の雰囲気はどこか浮き足だっている。
　今日は水曜日だから、授業はいつもより一時間少ない。
　昼休みが終わったあとの授業はホームルームで、一時間かけて文化祭の出し物を決める、とのことだ。
　くわえて明日は学校の創立記念日で休みなものだから、この四時限目が終われば、あとは休みに突入したも同然なのである。
　クラスの連中が今か今かと終了のベルを待っているのは当然といえた。
lines.label: s149
lines.maoEnglish:
Fourth period is Contemporary Society.
With lunch so close, the whole classroom has grown restless.
It is Wednesday, so we have one fewer lesson than usual.
After lunch comes homeroom, when we are supposedly spending an hour choosing our class project for the cultural festival.
Better still, tomorrow is the school’s founding anniversary, so once fourth period ends, the holiday has effectively begun.
No wonder everyone is waiting so eagerly for the bell.

The lesson passes without incident, and the day continues without the slightest irregularity.
Come to think of it, perhaps I am the strange one for sitting through class so peacefully after everything abnormal I have experienced.
Once school ends and night falls, I will be working with Arcueid again.
If I think about what that means, I probably have no business taking it this easy.

For some reason, Shiki Tohno is smiling as if he is enjoying himself.

“Arcueid.”
I really have lost my mind.
Now I am imagining her down in the rear courtyard, waving up at me and calling, “Yoo-hoo!”

I take back everything I just thought.

　声をかけて近寄っていく。
　先輩は立ち尽くしたまま、ずっとこっちを見つめていた。
「なにやってるんです、こんなところで」
「そういう遠野くんこそ、あんなところで何をしてたんですか？
　お昼休みは始まったばっかりなのに裏庭にいるなんて、四時限目をさぼっちゃったんですね」
「まさか。
ちょっとフライングして教室を出ただけだって」
　はあ、と先輩は気のない返事をする。
　いつもどおりの笑顔なんだけど、どうもこんな時間に裏庭にいた俺を訝しんでいるみたいだ。

evidence.mirrorMoon:
"---Senpai!"
I call out to her as I run.
Senpai simply stands there, watching me.
"What are you doing here?"
"The same for you, Tohno-kun.
What were you doing there?
Lunch has just began, so for you to be back here you must have skipped fourth period class."
"Of course not.
I just flew out of the classroom, that's all."
"Oh," Senpai answers without any enthusiasm.
It's her normal smile, but it seems like she's glaring at me.

lines.japanese:
……文化祭の出し物を決めるホームルームは、予想に反して難航した。
　様々な意見が飛びかい、教室中の全生徒の意見が対立した結果、決定は来週に延期になった。
　終わってみれば時計はとっくに夕方になっていて、みな疲れ果てた様子で教室を後にしていく。
「――――さて」
　教室でぼんやりとしていても仕方がない。
　夜にそなえて屋敷に戻るとしよう―――
lines.label: s153
lines.maoEnglish:
Contrary to all expectations, homeroom’s attempt to choose an attraction for the school festival dragged on.
Suggestions flew from every corner, the entire class split into opposing camps, and in the end the decision was postponed until next week.
By the time it was over, evening had long since arrived, and everyone filed out of the classroom looking exhausted.
“Well…”
There’s no point sitting here in a daze.
I should head back to the mansion and prepare for tonight—

"----Well then."
There's nothing to do in the classroom.
I should get ready for tonight and go back to the mansion---

「志貴さまさえよろしければ、夜に出掛ける事を秋葉さまにお隠しする事ができます」
「え？
　それって、つまり───口裏を合わせてくれるってこと？」
「───はい。
夕食後、秋葉さまはお部屋からお出になる事は稀です。
就寝前の見回りはわたしと姉さんがしておりますから、その報告に虚言をまぜてしまえば志貴さまが出掛けられた事は知られません」
lines.label: s154
lines.maoEnglish:
“Please wait.”
“…Forgive me for presuming.”
Hisui paused, clenched both hands, then made herself look directly at me.
“If you wish, Master Shiki, I can conceal your nightly outings from Miss Akiha.”
“What? You mean you’ll cover for me?”
“Yes. Miss Akiha rarely leaves her room after dinner. My sister and I conduct the final rounds before bedtime, so if we include a falsehood in our report, she will never know that Master Shiki left.”

これから殺し合いに行くっていう自覚がないみたいね、貴方には」
　ぷんぷん、という擬音が似合いそうなぐらい、アルクェイドはご機嫌ななめだ。

I’ll be punctual from now on, so let this one go.”
“Honestly. You don’t seem to understand that we’re about to go fight someone to the death.”
Arcueid was so cross that you could almost see her huffing in indignation.
Had she been waiting since long before our appointed time?

　アルクェイドは何も言わずに、何か目的でもあるように迷うことなく歩いていく。
　数時間かけて、街じゅうを歩きまわって。
　結局、ただの一つも、異状な『死』を内包した人間を見つける事はできなかった。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
We walked through the city at night.
Arcueid said nothing and moved without hesitation, as though she had a destination in mind.
We spent several hours ranging across the city.
In the end, we failed to find a single person who harbored an abnormal ‘death.’
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… We walk the nighttime streets.
Arcueid doesn't say anything, she just continues to stride forth resolutely.
We walk for hours in the midst of town.
In the end, we don't see one aberration, not one person wrapped in "death".
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「志貴、メガネをつけていいわ。
どうやら今夜は探し回っても無駄みたい」
　はあ、とため息をついて、アルクェイドは結論を下した。
　メガネをかける。
　視界が健全なものに戻って、ホッと胸を撫で下ろした。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, you can put your glasses back on. It looks like searching any longer tonight would be pointless.”
With a sigh, Arcueid pronounced the hunt over.
I put my glasses on.
My vision returned to sanity, and relief loosened my chest.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki, you can put your glasses back on.
It seems like no matter how much we search tonight, it'll be useless."
Arcueid concludes with a sigh.
I put my glasses back on.
My vision returns back to normal and I relax.

lines.japanese:
「今夜は無駄みたいって、そんな簡単に見きりをつけていいのかよ。
まだ一回しか街を見まわってないじゃないか」
「ううん、一回見まわれば十分よ。
気配っていうのはね、多少はその場所に残留するものなの。
今夜は死者の気配がどこにもなかったから、活動している死者はいないわ。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Pointless tonight? Aren’t you giving up awfully quickly? We’ve only made one circuit of the city.”
“No, once is enough. A presence leaves traces behind in a place. There was no trace of the Dead anywhere tonight, so none of them are active.”
lines.mao_english:
“Pointless tonight? Aren’t you giving up awfully quickly? We’ve only made one circuit of the city.”
“No, once is enough. A presence leaves traces behind in a place. There was no trace of the Dead anywhere tonight, so none of them are active.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Useless?
Is it okay to just decide that all of a sudden?
We've only looked everywhere once, right?"
"No, just once is enough.
The presence of The Dead tends to linger around a place.
I haven't sensed any of them around at all, so there aren't any that are active."

lines.japanese:
「……敵もほとんどの死者を倒されて警戒してるんでしょうね。
　まったく、どこまで小心者なんだか。
てっきり今晩あたりにでも決着をつけにくるって予想してたのに、まだ隠れんぼを続けたいみたい」
　アルクェイドは不満そうに唇を噛む。
「不機嫌そうだな、アルクェイド」
「当然でしょう。
せっかく志貴が手伝ってくれてるのに、これじゃ意味がないじゃない」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“The enemy must be wary after losing nearly all of the Dead under its control.
What a coward. I expected it to come settle matters tonight, but apparently it wants to keep playing hide-and-seek.”
Arcueid bit her lip in frustration.
“You look upset, Arcueid.”
“Of course I am. You went to all this trouble to help me, and it was completely wasted.”
lines.mao_english:

What a coward. I expected it to come settle matters tonight, but apparently it wants to keep playing hide-and-seek.”

“Of course I am. You went to all this trouble to help me, and it was completely wasted.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… The enemy is alert now that most of his Dead are defeated.
Seriously, he really is a coward.
I was so prepared to finish it all tonight, but it appears he still wants to play hide and seek."
Arcueid bites her lip, dissatisfied.
"You look like you're in a bad mood, Arcueid."
"Of course I am.
You went through such trouble to help me, but it's all meaningless now."

lines.japanese:
「――まあ、俺はかまわないんだけどさ。
そんなにご不満なら、もう一度街を見てまわってもかまわないよ。
俺も今度は意識を集中して視るからさ、もしかしたら何か見つけられるかもしれない」
「ダメよ。
これ以上志貴に無理はさせられない」
「無理って、別に俺は無理なんかしてないけど？」
「してるのよ。
志貴本人は気がついてないでしょうけど、これ以上脳を酷使したら廃人になりかねないわ」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“I don’t really mind. If you’re that dissatisfied, we can make another circuit. This time I’ll concentrate harder when I look. Maybe I’ll find something.”
“No. I’m not letting you push yourself any further.”
“Push myself? I’m not pushing myself at all.”
“You are. You may not notice it, but if you work your brain any harder, you could reduce yourself to a vegetable.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"--Well, I don't really mind.
If you're that dissatisfied, I don't mind going out to look again.
Maybe if I concentrate more we can find something."
"That's no good.
I can't strain you any more."
"Strain?
I'm not really straining."
"You are.
You might not realize it, but if you abuse your brain anymore, you might end up disabled."

lines.japanese:
「……？
　廃人って、誰が？」
「貴方がよ。
―――そっか、志貴は自分の目がどうゆうふうに働いているものだか知らないんだっけ」
「いい？
　志貴は生物の死は視やすくて、鉱物の死は視にくいって言ってたでしょ？
　それはね、結局は貴方の脳の回線の問題なの。
　モノの死。
その因果を視る、ということは、実際は見ているではなく読んでいる、という意味合いに近いわ」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“What…? Me?”
“You. That’s right—you don’t know how your eyes actually work, do you?”
“Listen carefully. You said the death of living creatures is easy to see, while the death of minerals is difficult, remember?
That comes down to the circuitry in your brain.
When you perceive the death of a thing—when you see the chain of cause and effect leading to its end—you aren’t truly looking at it so much as reading it.”
lines.mao_english:

That comes down to the circuitry in your brain.
When you perceive the death of a thing—when you see the chain of cause and effect leading to its end—you aren’t truly looking at it so much as reading it.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"……?
Disabled?
Who?"
"You.
---That's right, you don't exactly know how your eyes work."
"Okay?
You said yourself it was easier to see the death of living things than non-living things, right?
Basically, it's a problem of the circuitry of your brain.
The death of things.
Being able to see that cause and effect, it's closer to reading than seeing."

lines.japanese:
「……物事には大本になった原因、絶対の一があるの。
ええーと、ドイツの学者さんがアカシックレコードとか名づけたものと同じね。
　ようするに、事象の中心には『全てを記録したモノ』がある。
記録、というよりは『有る』ものだから、情報っていうわけじゃない。
ただ『有る』だけ。
それ自体に意思はないし、方向性もありえない。
　ただ原因を垂れ流しているだけの、根源の渦みたいなものね」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Everything has a first cause, an absolute One. It’s something like what a German scholar called the Akashic Records.
In other words, at the heart of all phenomena is ‘that which records everything.’ Though ‘record’ isn’t quite right, because it isn’t information. It simply exists. It has no will of its own, and no possible direction.
Think of it as a vortex at the Root that does nothing but spill causes into existence.”
lines.mao_english:

In other words, at the heart of all phenomena is ‘that which records everything.’ Though ‘record’ isn’t quite right, because it isn’t information. It simply exists. It has no will of its own, and no possible direction.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Everything has a main reason, the one source.
Um, it's the same thing that a German scientist called the Akashic Record.
In other words, in the core of all phenomenon, there is something that "records all things".
It's less of a record than an "existence", so it isn't information.
It just exists.
It doesn't have any purpose in and of itself, or any direction.
It's like a root swirl from which flows out all reasons."

lines.japanese:
「この世界にあるものは、その渦から流れ、派生して、今のカタチを保っている。
わたしも志貴も、吸血種も人間も、もとはそこから始まったものなの。
　……もう複雑に離れすぎてしまって、原因である始まりに戻ることはできないけど、とにかくそういった“一”があるのは分かるでしょう？
　
　でもね、たとえどんなに大本からかけ離れたカタチになってしまったとしても、そこから派生した存在である以上、とても細い線だけど糸はつながっているのよ」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Everything in this world flowed out of that vortex, branched away from it, and assumed its present form. You and I, humans and every vampiric species—we all began there.
We’ve grown too complex and wandered too far to return to that first cause, but you understand that this One exists, don’t you?
And however far a thing’s present form may have strayed from the source, if it arose from there, a thread still connects them—infinitely fine, but unbroken.”
lines.mao_english:
“Everything in this world flowed out of that vortex, branched away from it, and assumed its present form. You and I, humans and every vampiric species—we all began there.
We’ve grown too complex and wandered too far to return to that first cause, but you understand that this One exists, don’t you?
And however far a thing’s present form may have strayed from the source, if it arose from there, a thread still connects them—infinitely fine, but unbroken.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Things in this world flowed from that, derived from that, and preserve their current form.
You and I, vampires and humans, we all originated from that.
…… Things became more complex and separate, and cannot return to that original source, the beginning.
But you understand that there exists "The One", right?
But, no matter how different a form something takes from the great source, it is still a derivative.
So even if it is only a slender line, there is a thread connecting to the source."

lines.japanese:
「全ての根源、全ての始まりと終わりを記録したレコード。
それと繋がっているものは、物事の終わりを『識っている』ことになる。
　もともと脳っていうのは受信と送信をつかさどる機能なんだけど、たいていの人間はみんなその回線が自分に対してのみで閉じてしまっている。
　けど、中には潜在的に回線が開けてしまっている人間がいるわ。
なんの魔術回路も利用せず、超越種でさえないのに超常現象を可能とする人間。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“The Root of everything: a record containing every beginning and every end. Anything connected to it ‘knows’ how things end.
The brain is fundamentally an organ for transmitting and receiving, but in most people its circuitry is closed upon the self.
But some people are born with those circuits open. They can cause supernatural phenomena without using a single Magic Circuit, despite not belonging to any transcendent species.”
lines.mao_english:
“The Root of everything: a record containing every beginning and every end. Anything connected to it ‘knows’ how things end.
The brain is fundamentally an organ for transmitting and receiving, but in most people its circuitry is closed upon the self.
But some people are born with those circuits open. They can cause supernatural phenomena without using a single Magic Circuit, despite not belonging to any transcendent species.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"The source of all things, the record that records the beginning and the end of all things.
Being connected to that means knowing the end of all things.
Originally the brain has the ability to control reception and transmission, but most humans close off all of these circuits except for themselves.
But, there are those people who have their circuits open latently.
Without a single use of Magic Circuits, there are humans who, despite not being of a transcendental race, have the potential to create transcendent phenomena.

lines.japanese:
「これをね、魔術師たちは超能力者って区分している。
人間でありながら、生まれついて何らかの魔術回路そのものという突然変異体。
―――例えば何の神秘も学んでいないのに『物の死』を視てしまう人間とか、ね」
「――――――」
　……いや、申し訳ないんだけど、アルクェイド。
　せっかくのお話を、どうも俺の脳みそはまったく理解してくれてなさそうだ。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Mages classify those people as psychics. They’re human mutants born as something equivalent to a Magic Circuit in their own right.
―――Someone who can see the ‘death of things’ without ever studying the mysteries, for example.”
“…”
I was sorry, Arcueid, truly.
But despite all the trouble she had taken, my brain seemed to have understood none of that whatsoever.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Magi classify them as being psychics.
While still human, they are mutants who are born with Magic Circuits.
---Such as, without any learning of the occult, someone who can see the 'death of things'."
"------"
…… Um, I'm sorry, Arcueid.
It appears I can't understand this kind of conversation at all.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Arcueid distinguishes psychics as human mutations born as some form of magical circuit itself, capable of the supernatural without employing ordinary Magic Circuits. mirror moon says merely that they are born with Magic Circuits, collapsing the exception into the normal magus mechanism and contradicting the immediately preceding statement that they use no magical circuit.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: A psychic whose body is itself a magical circuit becomes someone born with circuits

lines.japanese:
「いいわよ、志貴は理解なんかしなくて。
　ただ言っておきたいのは、あんまり視えにくいモノを自分から視ようとしちゃダメっていうこと。
　たぶん、志貴はその気になれば鉱物の『死』を確実に視るコトができる。
　けどそのために脳が生物という範疇から鉱物の範疇に回線を開いて、鉱物の死を識ろうとしてしまう。
―――それは、本来ありえない運動よ。
　だから脳が過負荷をおこして、志貴は間違いなく使い物にならなくなる」
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s fine. You don’t need to understand.
What you do need to remember is never to force yourself to see the death of something that won’t come into focus.
If you truly tried, you could probably see the ‘death’ of minerals with perfect clarity.
But to do it, your brain would have to open its circuitry beyond living things and into the category of minerals, then attempt to comprehend mineral death.
―――That operation should be impossible.
Your brain would overload, and you would unquestionably destroy yourself.”
lines.mao_english:

Your brain would overload, and you would unquestionably destroy yourself.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"It's okay if you can't understand.
But what I want to tell you is you shouldn't try to see things that are hard to see.
Probably, if you want to, you can see the "death" of non-living things.
But in order to do that, your brain has to open its circuits from the classification of living things to the classification of non-living things in order to understand.
---That is normally an impossible process.
As a result, it overloads your brain, and you'll end up being useless."

lines.japanese:
「使い物にならなくなるって―――その、この目が死を視なくなってくれるっていう事？」
「―――まさか。
ねえ志貴、無理をしてオーバーブロウしたエンジンっていうのはどうなるかしら」
「そりゃあジャンク行きだろ。
一度でも壊れたエンジンは二度と使い物にならな――――」
　ああ、そういうコト。
　つまりは、死を見ている時の頭痛は、スピードをあげすぎて悲鳴をあげているエンジンと同じだったのか。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“Destroy myself… Do you mean these eyes would stop seeing death?”
“Of course not. Shiki, what happens to an engine that’s pushed until it blows?”
“It goes to the scrapyard. Once an engine breaks, it’s never useful again—”
Oh. So that was what she meant.
The headaches I felt when I looked at death were like an engine screaming because it had been driven too fast.

"Useless---you mean, these eyes won't be able to perceive death anymore?"
"---Of course not.
Hey Shiki, what happens to an engine that blows up from overload?"
"It goes to the junk yard.
Once an engine breaks, you can't use it agai----"
Oh, that's it.
In other words, the headache I get from seeing death is like the screaming of an engine that is working too fast.

「わかった？
　ただ視えているだけなら問題はないでしょうけど、視えないモノを視ようとするのだけは止めて。
脳内の血管が破裂して、それこそ取り返しのつかない事になるから」
　……言葉がない。
　そんな大変なことを知らずに、俺は今まで生きてきたっていうんだ。
lines.label: s156
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
“Do you understand now? Merely seeing what presents itself should be safe, but never strain to see what you can’t. A blood vessel in your brain could rupture, and then there would be no undoing the damage.”
I had no answer.
I had lived all this time without knowing something so serious.
